name: Bromhexine

overview.mechanism: Helps alter bronchial mucus characteristics to facilitate clearance of secretions. [[BROM-TRIAL,BROM-EMA]]
uses: Symptomatic mucus clearance in respiratory disease; indications and age restrictions depend on the product. [[BROM-TRIAL,BROM-EMA]]

evidence.title: Respiratory evidence: modest and older trials

paragraphs.text: A small double-blind crossover study enrolled 41 patients with chronic bronchitis and irreversible airflow obstruction; 36 were included in the reported analysis. Bromhexine reduced patient-rated phlegm stickiness and improved physician-rated overall clinical state, but did not significantly improve cough, breathlessness, sputum volume or measured airflow. All participants also received oxytetracycline, limiting generalization to current routine care.

EMA required safety information concerning severe cutaneous adverse reactions, including erythema multiforme, Stevens–Johnson syndrome/toxic epidermal necrolysis and acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis. Progressive rash, particularly with blistering or mucosal lesions, warrants immediate discontinuation and medical advice. Anaphylactic reactions, including shock and angioedema, are also included in the safety amendments.

The cited chronic-bronchitis trial did not establish a CKD adjustment or dialysis regimen. Symptomatic mucus improvement should not be presented as a kidney benefit. Current product-specific renal precautions and formulation details should be checked rather than inferred from the mucolytic drug class.

sources.citation: A controlled trial of bromhexine (Bisolvon) in out-patients with chronic bronchitis. PubMed PMID: 1095307.
European Medicines Agency. Ambroxol and bromhexine: Article 31 referral, Annex III, product-information safety amendments.
